descriptors.definition: External chartered accountant firms performing concurrent audits receive compensation determined by the bank's Audit Committee. This financial remuneration considers factors such as workload area coverage, required technical skill sets, staff numbers, and allocated audit time.
inclusion: Fixation of fees based on area coverage and staffing
Determination of compensation by the bank's ACB
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general bank employee remuneration and statutory audit fee determinations.

descriptors.definition: Concurrent auditors must utilize structured formats to document and communicate their findings to branch management, controlling offices, and the Audit Committee. Major deficiencies, minor irregularities, and fraudulent transactions require distinct escalation pathways and immediate corrective follow-up actions.
inclusion: Immediate reporting of fraud to the Chief Vigilance Officer and Head Office
Quarterly reviews submitted to the Audit Committee
Discussion of important issues with the branch manager prior to report submission
exclusion: General statutory audit reporting under company law standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard internal audit reviews by its emphasis on immediate fraud escalation and concurrent quarterly compliance tracking.

descriptors.definition: Banks establish a board-level oversight committee following regulatory guidelines to direct and evaluate the entire internal inspection and audit network. This committee specifically reviews auditor appointments, fee structures, audit quality, and implementation efficacy of follow-up corrective measures.
inclusion: Reviewing the appointment systems and remuneration of concurrent auditors
Periodical meetings with concurrent and statutory auditors
exclusion: Direct execution of field audit verification tests
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from executive branch management by its governance role focused on oversight, review, and direction of audit systems.
